_: WHERE A TASK IS UP TO, once (the owner, 2026-10-26: 'are these modes defined well anywhere besides the UI, how the parts of the UI display and what is hidden - we should define this well'). Read by the task page (website/src/stages.js), the server's task detail and the Assistant's CANVAS block (taskuary/stages.py). `rules` decide the stage: the first whose fact holds wins, each side reading the facts its own way - the page from what it is drawing (a live terminal, the white section), the server from the task's rows - and the order is the one both keep. `stages` are the parts each stage draws: `main` the view the task opens on ('work': the agent's chat is the page, Came from the left drawer; 'task': what came in is the page, the chat beside it); `shows` what that view holds, in a sentence; `drawer` the other part and what is in it; `lit` whether that part's tab is lit because the next move is inside it; `advisor` where the Advisor's line stands ('main' over the work, 'drawer' beside it, null: none on a closed task); `verbs` the moves the stage is about, by their buttons.json ids, first the one it is for. `section`: which of the task's two sections - 'from' (Came from) or 'agent' (the one chat, where every draft, Send and close is) - the task opens on (the owner, 2026-11-06: 'there should no longer be close out code anywhere ... now that even coding agents using one agent tab'). Every kind but a plain to-do opens on its chat whatever the stage; a to-do opens where its stage says.

rules._: an agent's session is open - working, or waiting on you at its prompt
handed to a person: nothing is yours until they answer
closed by its own agent: who closed it and why are the chat's (trust audit S2, 2026-10-28)
a draft or emails wait for Send in the chat, something already went out, or a write-up failed
an agent finished, stopped or failed, and its Result (or why it failed) is the move
somebody wrote and is owed a reply, nothing drafted yet
a to-do's checklist or a goal's steps are the move
an ask nothing has worked yet - the agent is the move
